title: Tenant Management Data System
description: The Tenant Housing Data Management System is designed to facilitate efficient management of tenant information, particularly for Section 8 housing. The system's primary objective is to securely store and manage tenant data while providing functionalities for monitoring digital card balances and automating notifications regarding remaining balances. It encompasses the storage and management of various tenant details, including names, contact information, and digital card balances, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and data protection standards.User management features include support for multiple user roles, such as tenants and management, each with specific permissions and access levels, enforced through robust user authentication mechanisms. Tenants are empowered to create and maintain their profiles with accurate and up-to-date information, including mandatory fields like full name, contact information, and Section 8 identification number, with optional fields for address and emergency contact details.The system effectively tracks and manages digital card balances associated with each tenant, allowing management to update balances manually or automatically based on transactions. Furthermore, it supports automated notifications to alert both tenants and management regarding digital card balances, with tenants receiving alerts via text message or email when their balance falls below a predetermined threshold, and management receiving notifications concerning low balances and overdue payments.In addition to functional requirements, non-functional aspects such as security, performance, and reliability are of paramount importance. The system must comply with industry-standard security protocols to protect sensitive PII data, including encryption for data transmission and storage, along with access controls to prevent unauthorized access. It must also be capable of efficiently handling a large volume of tenant data and transactions, with acceptable response times and scalability to accommodate future growth. Reliability is ensured through built-in redundancy, backup mechanisms, and regular maintenance to proactively address potential issues.The system's architecture is structured around a relational database to optimize data storage and retrieval, with a modular and scalable application architecture utilizing a combination of frontend and backend technologies. The user interface design prioritizes user-friendliness and responsiveness, providing intuitive navigation and clear layouts for managing profiles and monitoring digital card balances.Legal and compliance considerations include adherence to requirements for handling personal data and compliance with Section 8 regulations governing housing programs, ensuring data retention policies are established to align with program requirements. An implementation plan outlines development phases from requirements analysis to deployment, with comprehensive testing strategies to validate the system against requirements. Ongoing maintenance and technical support are essential for addressing bugs, security vulnerabilities, and user inquiries efficiently, ensuring the system's continued reliability and performance.

title: Schedule Variance  and Estimated at Completion Dashboard - Excel = Better planning and forecasting
description: I am seeking a data analyst to develop a sophisticated productivity calculator designed to accurately predict the necessary daily work hours and overall timeline required to complete projects based on various productivity levels and working conditions. The core functionality of this calculator should hinge on analyzing and integrating several key variables: the total project hours needed for completion, the productivity rate of the crew (expressed as a percentage reflecting the actual productive hours out of a standard workday), the size of the crew involved, and the flexibility in working days per week (ranging from a traditional 5-day workweek to extended options of 6 or even 4 days, adjusting for longer or shorter weeks). This tool must adeptly handle the calculation of required daily productive hours for the crew as a whole, taking into account the specified productivity rate, which can vary from 82% (where, for example, out of an 8-hour day, 6.56 hours are effectively productive) to a maximum of 94%. It should provide adjustable parameters for the analyst to simulate different scenarios, such as increasing the workday length to 9 hours or modifying the workweek, and calculate the impact of these adjustments on meeting the project deadline. Crucially, the calculator must offer insights into how changes in daily productivity affect the overall project timeline and suggest optimal working conditions to ensure project completion within the desired timeframe. By inputting different productivity rates, crew sizes, and working conditions, the tool should be able to forecast the total number of working days required to meet the project goal of, say, 1300 hours, and recommend adjustments to daily working hours or crew productivity rates necessary to achieve this target on time. This functionality will be instrumental in planning and decision-making processes, allowing for precise adjustments to work schedules, resource allocation, or project scope as needed to ensure timely and efficient project delivery. The end product should be a user-friendly, interactive calculator that enables quick scenario testing and provides clear, actionable output to guide project managers in optimizing their team's work schedule and productivity strategies for on-time project completion.  Schedule Variance Dashboard

title: RADIUS Proxy server in multi realm environment
description: We are looking for someone to assist with setting up a RADIUS proxy server. We currently operate a large number of BNGs (NAS devices) which all need to authenticate RADIUS/PPP requests to RADIUS servers. The number of realms being matched is increasing, as well as the number of NAS devices. It is not feasible to keep updating NAS devices on each radius server.For each @realm.tld RADIUS request, the BNG will look up the respective realm, and then query that specific RADIUS server for AAA information (Mikrotik PPPOE Authentication). The RADIUS server will return: IP Address and Up/Down Rate limit. NAS device will send usage/uptime stats to RADIUS server periodically.We require a RADIUS Proxy server, based on FreeRADIUS. This proxy server will now handle the @realm.tld lookup and request AAA from the respective RADIUS server. Our NAS devices will send all radius requests to this Proxy server, which will in turn query the respective RADIUS server, and return Authentication, IP and usage information as required.We will provide two Linx (any flavour) servers, with public IP addresses. A working RADIUS proxy server that proxies requests based on @realm.tld (proxy realms) needs to be configured. Our multiple BNGs (NAS devices) will send all RADIUS requests to either of these two Proxy RADIUS servers, the NAS IP will need to be re-written to match the Proxy, and the request sent to the respective RADIUS. Responses will need to be sent to the correct NAS, and AAA/PPPOE connections established.Possible betterment/additional scope: Including a GUI to manage realms (basically write to proxy.conf file) as well as RADIUS servers and NAS devices.

title: Marketplace Purchase Automation (Bypass Cloudflare)
description: Script Purpose:I have a Puppeteer script that combines with a private google chrome extension (to avoid Cloudflare detection) to automate the purchase of newly listed items on an online marketplace if certain values are met.The Process:Script reads newly listed items via websocket API, if the newly listed item(s) matches the filters I have set - the script will attempt to purchase them. The script adds the items to the cart, redirects to the checkout page, the payment form appears, and then attempts order creation via web request. During order creation, the script solves the Cloudflare turnstile to send the request.Current Problem:Bypassing Cloudflare and generating a valid token, the marketplace is currently detecting the generated token as they depend on other values, parameters, or requests which are uncertain. The token should be provided as a parameter on the order creation payload for the website to create the order. The script currently bypasses the Cloudflare turnstile, but it is likely the issue is not related to the turnstile part as the script can already generate the token with no issue, it's about other parameters or requests.Currently this process methodology is very slow, it takes the script roughly 5-6 seconds to complete a successful order. The primary slow speed comes from the payment form loading (likely related to website server connection). Once the payment form loads it then has to solve the cloudflare turnstile, and finally attempts to submit the request for the order. Newly listed items are limited in small quantities (typically 1-3), meaning if another user on the website submits the order before the script, the error “This item is no longer in your cart” appears. Current competition is able to create orders within 2 seconds, making it nearly impossible to get successful orders. title: Python Senior Developer for creating documents based on document comparison
description: OverviewWe have a software tool that compares two text documents, referred to as the "left" document and the "right" document. These documents can be in PDF, DOC, or DOCX format. The tool lets users analyze differences and decide whether to accept or reject these changes. After reviewing, users can create a new DOCX file that includes the accepted edits and marks the undecided changes with special tags (like 'w:ins' for added text or 'w:del' for deleted text). This new document starts as a copy of the right document, but it will use text from the left document where changes were not accepted. Any changes not decided upon will appear as open edits in Microsoft Word.What We NeedWe want to make a new tool or script that can take a list of changes (in a file called changeList.json) from our comparison tool and apply those changes correctly in a new third DOCX document, based on what users have accepted or rejected. To keep things straightforward, we will only provide DOCX files for comparison.The changeList.json file records all differences spotted by our tool. Differences include:Match: Text is the same in both documents.Insert: New text appears in the second document.Delete: Text from the first document is missing in the second.Replace: Text from the first document is changed in the second.Here’s an example of what the change list might contain:["kind": "match","text": "Documento"// ... more info here,"kind": "replace","leftText": "S","rightText": "s","status": "pending"// ... more info here// ... more changes listed]Consider any change not marked with status as pendingWhen applying a 'replace' action in the DOCX, it should be formatted like this:[w:del] ... [w:t]S[/w:t] ... [/w:del][w:ins] ... [w:t]s[/w:t] ... [/w:ins]If a user rejects a change, the original text (leftText) takes the place of the changed text (rightText) in the new document. If a change involves deleting text, that text should go back where it was originally, with the same style and format.The ChallengeThe main difficulty lies in transferring these changes into the third document when they involve tables. It's especially hard with tables that have removed rows and columns, or when cells are joined together or there are tables within tables. We'll provide example documents that include these tricky situations to help you understand what needs to be done.There are no strict rules about which technologies you must use, but our system works on Linux containers and we use Python. Your new tool or script must work within this environment. It should be able to run on Linux containers and be callable from Python code.

title: update the attached NinjaTrader 8 MACD crossover strategy
description: Entry Logic: The attached MACD strategy checks for MACD crossover signals using the CrossAbove and CrossBelow methods. A bullish crossover occurs when the MACD line crosses above the signal line. A bearish crossover occurs when the MACD line crosses below the signal line. These crossover signals are filtered based on the trend direction indicated by the Chandelier Stop indicator. For a bullish crossover, the strategy enters a long position (EnterLong) only if the trend indicated by the Chandelier Stop is  downward. For a bearish crossover, the strategy enters a short position (EnterShort) only if the trend indicated by the Chandelier Stop is  upward.Position Management: The strategy manages positions by checking the current market position (Position.MarketPosition) before entering trades to avoid doubling up on positions or exiting positions prematurely. If a long position is already open (MarketPosition.Long) and a bearish crossover occurs, the strategy exits the long position (ExitLong) to capture profits or limit losses. If a short position is already open (MarketPosition.Short) and a bullish crossover occurs, the strategy exits the short position (ExitShort) to manage risk.I would like to update the attached MACD Crossover strategy with the following functions and parameters:1)Replace the MACD crossover exit with a Hard target exit - instead of using a macd crossover to exit an existing position (see "position management" above for more detail) I would like the strategy to exclusively replace this with a hard target in "x"ticks as the exit when the strategy hits its profit target. The hard target is entered when the strategy enters a position.2)Replace the MACD crossover exit with  a Hard Stop in "x" ticks - instead of using a macd crossover to exit an existing position (see "position management" above for more detail) I would like the strategy to  use a hard stop in "x"ticks as the exit. The hard stop is entered when the strategy enters a position.3)Add max trades per direction with an Enable/Disable parameter - The MaxTradesDirection parameter is used to limit the number of trades that can be taken in a particular direction (long or short). It uses the Chandelier stop to determine the trend direction. Let's say MaxTradesDirection is set to 1. This means that the strategy will only take one trade (either long or short) before waiting for the trend direction in the Chandelier stop to change before taking another trade in the same direction.For example: If MaxTradesDirection is set to 1, the strategy will not take another long trade until the current one is closed or exited. While the current long trade is active, the Chandelier Stop may continue to indicate an uptrend, but the strategy will not enter additional long trades due to the MaxTradesDirection limit. Once the current long trade is closed or exited (e.g., by hitting the fixed target or stop loss), the strategy will wait for a Chandelier Stop trend direction change before considering another long trade.I have attached the parameter list along with the strategy file.

title: WordPress Plugin Development for Backlinks
description: Looking to develop a Backlink Network plugin.When installed, it will create a dashboard for the user.  The dashboard will contain a number of tabs.1. 1st tab will display a list of all pages/posts on the WordPress site. It will contain Page Title, Keyword Focus from Yoast and URL. It will also show how many backlinks have been added to this URL from the backlink network.2. 2nd tab will contain Inventory of Pages/Posts in the Network inventory.3. Each WordPress site will gain backlink credits. When installed they will receive 2 free credits. This will be displayed at the top of the dashboard.4. The website owner will review the Network Inventory and select a keyword + URL, then manually add to a page/post.  Once added, they will return to the inventory + submit for review by providing the URL where the link was added.5. The plugin will verify the link exists and then send backlink details (URL + keyword) to Network Inventory.6. The network inventory database will have a backlink record for each URL and then update the backlink count on the inventory.7. When a site receives a backlink the dashboard will display a backlink count on the Site Page/Post in the 1st tab above.8. For every 2 backlinks added, the website will earn 1 backlink credit to be used in the 1st tab above.9. From the 1st tab, the user will select Pages/Posts to be displayed in the network inventory based on the number of backlink credits available. To start each user will receive 2 free credits. Each time they add 2 backlinks they will earn 1 more credit.10. A user can remove backlinks from their site, this will adjust their link credits and auto adjust which posts/pages display in the network inventory. This should be rescanned daily.11. If a user does not want to earn backlink credits, they can purchase.12. User can change which Pages/Posts they wish to include in the inventory at any time by selecting/unselecting from 1st tab even if they have received backlinks.13. To earn credits, a maximum of 3 backlinks will be allowed per URL. When scanning URL for backlinks to verify credits it should be based on a date the backlink was added. Therefore oldest backlinks should be counted 1st, any new links will not be counted after 3/URL.14. Backlinks added will required rel=dofollow to be counted for credit. When re-scanning backlinks daily, it should monitor for valid parameters.Will need the plugin maintained over time and help submitting to WordPress plugin directory. The initial plugin will not offer option to buy credits, we will add this in the future.

title: Re-implement StreamDiffusion POC
description: See https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U82LQtQbydvW8vT86GGD8m5-kCdKCZ2rEBD9VlVugUs/edit?usp=sharingIn short:Project OpenDiffusion: Reimplementing and improving stream diffusionWhile the proposed stream diffusion greatly improves speed over other diffusion approaches which makes interactivity and live generation possible, it also severely reduces creative freedom and is constrained to diffusing incoming video. The initial stream diffusion project is also an introduction to a concept, rather than a mature implementation of the potential of the concept. In this project, we aim to reimplement the stream diffusion concepts from the paper into “OpenDiffusion”.In this first POC, we will experiment with different changes to the pipelines to enable more creative freedom at the expense of speed and efficiently,  but retain the continuous streaming nature. Additionally, introducing Prompt Arrangement Clips (PAC) as a mechanism to drive changing text prompt input and other controls and variables to steer continuous generation in “dream mode” or otherwise. The implementation re-introduces negative prompts into continuous diffusion.

title: Back and forward test trading bot
description: Will need the following. With reports to confirm the potential of the trading bot. May require more than one to be checked.Backtesting:Collect Historical Data: Obtain historical price data for the cryptocurrency pairs you want to trade. Binance provides historical data through their API or you can use third-party sources.Implement Trading Strategy: Modify your trading bot code to run in a backtesting environment. Instead of fetching real-time data, simulate the trading decisions based on historical data.Set Up Backtesting Framework: Create a framework to simulate trades based on historical data. This can involve iterating through historical data, applying your trading strategy, and keeping track of simulated trades and portfolio value.Run Backtest: Execute the backtesting framework with your modified trading bot code. Monitor the bot's performance, including metrics such as profit/loss, win rate, drawdown, and Sharpe ratio.Analyze Results: Analyze the results of the backtest to evaluate the performance of your trading bot. Identify strengths and weaknesses, and consider making adjustments to the trading strategy or parameters based on the insights gained.Forward Testing:Set Up Paper Trading Account: Create a paper trading account on Binance or use their API sandbox environment. This will allow you to trade with virtual funds in real-time market conditions without risking real money.Deploy Trading Bot: Deploy your trading bot in the paper trading environment. Ensure that it's connected to the paper trading account and configured to execute trades using virtual funds.Monitor Performance: Monitor the performance of your trading bot in the paper trading environment. Keep track of trades executed, portfolio value, and performance metrics.Evaluate Results: Evaluate the performance of your trading bot in the paper trading environment. Compare its performance to the results of the backtest and identify any discrepancies or issues.Optimize and Refine: Based on the results of forward testing, optimize and refine your trading bot as necessary. This may involve tweaking parameters, adjusting the trading strategy, or implementing additional risk management techniques.Gradual Deployment: Once you're confident in the performance of your trading bot in the paper trading environment, you can consider deploying it with a small amount of real funds in a live trading environment on Binance.

Although this can be switched in the plugin's settings, it does not work for a multi-user setup of webhosting companies as some clients wish to reply from the custom email address which is the current default setting while others want to reply from their regular identity/address. This means, there needs to be a toggle in Roundcube's settings to choose one or the other option.→ Can this option be added to Roundcube's UI settings when adding the plugin?→ An even better solution may be to integrate half of the functionality in Roundcube natively by making the local-part of the email address editable. A toggle option in the settings shall determine to either always reply with the default identity or with the custom local-part the email was sent to before is got forwarded to the mailbox (as long as the domain-part is the same. Otherwise, it would require the custom_from plugin for a totally virtual alias). This saves setting up several identities for each custom email address the user receives emails to.The benefit is to communicate with each service provider by an individual email address so when the personal email address is leaked, it can easily be blocked by filtering as the main mailbox remains unknown which is a great spam protection.2) The plugin loses the modified email address and switched back to the user's default identity when saving a draft, closing the editing window and reopening the draft.→ Can this be fixed?You would need to set up a Roundcube installation and test the changes before creating a pull request on GitHub.Also modify the plugin's (and i.a.
